text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Slovenia loses case against Beogradska Banka Cyprus.
- Wheat crop this year above three million tonnes which is a 25-year record high, said Serbian Agriculture Minister Jovan Babovic.
- Some 873 kilometres of main, regional and local roads are under construction in Serbia this year, said Svetolik Kostadinovic, republic's Minister for Transport and Communications.
- Yugoslav river shippers doubled the quantity of transported goods in the first six months this year compared to the same period in 1996, said the company's general director Dusan Strugar.
- Yugoslav January-June exports were 21 percent and imports 11 percent below plan, said the Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce and Industry.
- New import duties burden domestic industries and additionally increase production cost, businessmen say.
- The main board of the opposition Serbian Renewal Movement to decide soon if the party will participate coming elections.

- Victory of the Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic at republic's presidental elections would bring into question existance of the federation, said Vojislav Seselj leader of the Serbian Radical Party.
NASA BORBA

- U.S. special representative for implementation of the Dayton accords Robert Gelbard and former Bosnia peace negotiator Richard Holbrooke will arrive to Belgrade with an ultimatum to Yugoslav President Slobodan Milosevic - strict implementation of Dayton peace agreement or face fresh economic sanctions.
- Some hundred arms factory workers of Kragujevac began a march to Belgrade against poverty and humiliation.
- OSCE says Serbian authorities did not provide adequate conditions for their observers to be present at coming September 21 elections.
- The Hague war crimes tribunal should be turned into committee for gathering evidence, said Momcilo Krajisnik, Bosnian Serb representative in the Bosnian presidency.
- Coalition of Vojvodina criticizes Belgrade oposition and says boycott of the elections would be a historical mistake.
- Serbian Commodity Reserves Agency will provide some million tonnes of beef, 800 tonnes of pork and 200 tonnes of chicken meat to overcome current market shortages.
BORBA
- Multilateral compensation have reduced registerd internal debt of 39.8 billion dinars by 14,5 percent, the central bank said.
- Copper production in Serbia's mining and smelting complex Bor increased by 19 percent in January-July over the same period in 1996, said deputy production director Zivorad Stanisavljevic.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA
- The congress held in Kolasin on Wednesday is not the congress of the the Montenegrin ruling Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS), said Dragan Djurovic, high DPS official.

- If Montenegrin opposition fails to agree on a single presidental candidate, the Peoples Party will have its own candidate for republic's presidental elections on October 5, said party leader Novak Kilibarda.
